page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile for this hardware configuration. The instance achieves average single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, but its multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 13.86 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 11.77 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks register in the bottom 10%, while single-core Geekbench and PassMark memory scores fall into the bottom 25% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. Due to its low multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, it is best suited for lightweight database operations, basic caching layers, or small-scale web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw computational throughput.
